back: A unit of product or service to which costs are traced, such as a loaf, a job or a kilometre.
A department, section, machine or activity where costs are collected before they are charged to cost units.
A direct cost can be traced economically to one cost unit; an indirect cost (overhead) cannot.
Direct materials + direct labour + direct expenses.
Product costs (direct costs plus production overheads) go into inventory until sale. Period costs (selling, distribution, administration) are charged to the period.
A future cash cost that changes because of a decision. Sunk costs and unchanged apportioned costs are irrelevant.
The benefit given up by choosing one course of action instead of the next best alternative.
A cost already incurred that cannot be changed by any decision now; ignore it in decisions.
Cost control, pricing, inventory valuation and decision making.
Cost accounting records and analyses costs; management accounting uses them with budgets and forecasts for planning, control and decisions, for internal use only.
